note: City of Osage park on the Cedar River, with primitive camping on the wooded high ground above the river; toilets, and drinking water from the namesake spring. Minimal hookups; confirm electric on arrival. Open about April to November. The sites have not been confirmed at the waterline. --Claude
summary: The City of Osage pages confirm Spring Park as a 'primitive camping area' with a tested drinking-water spring (and list '1 primitive campground (Spring Park)'). They give no rate, site count, rig length, season or booking rule. Potable water confirmed; not waterfront stands; the website should be the city page, not allstays.

PHONE missing: City of Osage 641-732-3709 (city site footer: 'Phone: 641-732-3709', 806 Main Street). The Google result for 'Spring Park Osage' resolved to Mitchell County's Cedar Bridge Park instead, so there is no separate park listing.

WATERFRONT: 'not waterfront' stands, re-audited both ways. The Cedar is about 60-70 m wide here (river-sized) and the park road loops within about 30-50 m of the bank, with an open dirt and grass apron reaching the bank at ~43.2749,-92.8518 (likely the fishing/river access area the city lists). No camping pads or RVs can be told apart on either image, so a waterfront value cannot be earned. A 2019 camper review (ParkAdvisor, secondary) says 'trees and underbrush block the view of the river'. Downgrade rule: stays at not waterfront.
